_comment: Gold question -> acceptable-chunk-marker pairs for the retrieval harness.
EVERY marker is a verbatim substring of the committed test corpus
(evaluator/test_content/generate_test_files.py), so a miss always means retrieval failed
to surface text that demonstrably exists in the index -- never that the label was wrong.
Markers are ANY-OF: the same fact appears in several chunks, and finding any one of them
is a legitimate retrieval. Matching also searches parent_text and snippet, because a
marker phrase can straddle a chunk boundary.
SCOPE: only the three LOCAL files (PDF/PPTX/DOCX) are labelled. The YouTube and Wikipedia
sources in the corpus are fetched live and their text can change, which would turn a
content edit upstream into a phantom retrieval regression.
PRIVACY: this file is COMMITTED to a PUBLIC repo. Never add pairs derived from the user's
real notebooks. Local pairs belong in <data_dir>/eval/retrieval_gold.local.json, which the
runner merges automatically and which lives outside the repo.
The 2026-08-21 research called for 60-120 pairs. This is a starting set built against the
corpus that already ships; grow it as real field questions get promoted.

questions.question: What embedding model does LocalBook use and how many dimensions does it produce?
How many parameters does the embedding model have?
How large are document chunks and how much do they overlap?
markers: passages of approximately 512 tokens with 50-token overlap

questions.question: Does chunking split on character counts or on structure?
markers: uses semantic boundaries (paragraphs, headers) rather than fixed character counts

questions.question: What are the layers of the system architecture?
markers: Intelligence Layer: RAG engine, context builder
Storage Layer: LanceDB for vector embeddings

questions.question: Which database stores the vector embeddings?
markers: Vectors are stored in LanceDB, an embedded vector database

questions.question: What are the steps of the RAG pipeline when a user asks a question?
markers: Embeds the query using the Snowflake Arctic Embed 2 model
Builds an adaptive context window based on available token budget

questions.question: How are retrieved results reranked?
markers: Top-k results are reranked using cross-encoder scoring

questions.question: Which model handles complex reasoning and document generation?
markers: Main Model (gemma4:e4b): Handles complex reasoning, document generation

questions.question: What context window does the main model run with?
markers: Runs with a context window of up to 16384

questions.question: What is the fast model used for?
markers: Used for quick tasks like intent classification, follow-up

questions.question: How many parameters does the fast model have and under what licence?
Does the system need a separate vision model?
markers: no separate vision model is required by default

questions.question: What throughput does the main model achieve on an Apple M4?
What MTEB information-retrieval score did Snowflake Arctic Embed 2 achieve?
What MTEB score and throughput did Nomic Embed Text reach?
How many documents were used to evaluate the embedding models?
markers: 500 documents (research papers, web articles, and technical documentation)

questions.question: Which embedding model was recommended and why?
markers: Snowflake Arctic Embed 2 provides the best balance of quality and efficiency
best balance of quality and efficiency

questions.question: How much memory does the arctic embedding model use during inference?
How does the context builder decide what to include?
markers: adaptive context builder manages the token budget
Retrieval chunks are prioritized by relevance score

questions.question: How much faster is Metal GPU acceleration than CPU inference?
markers: Metal GPU acceleration provides ~2x speedup over CPU inference

questions.question: What source metadata is kept for citation tracking?
markers: Source metadata (filename, page) is included for citation tracking
